disease_label_per_paper: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome due to Streptococcus pyogenes cellulitis
presentation_summary: 65-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes and peripheral arterial disease presented with fever, pain and swelling in the left leg worsening over three days.
Emergency department exam showed temperature 38.7 C, heart rate 108/min, blood pressure 85/52 mmHg, and clear inflammatory signs in the left leg.
Initial labs showed CRP 582 mg/L and creatinine 3 mg/dL; blood gas showed compensated metabolic acidosis.
CT of abdomen, pelvis and left leg showed moderate edema adjacent to the left femoral and iliac vessels.
He progressed to respiratory, hemodynamic, renal and neurologic dysfunction requiring mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy and vasopressors; SOFA score was 7 at ICU admission.
